title: Peak Identification of Cyanocobalamin According to USP 35-NF 30 S2
locator: Page 1, Equipment and Sample preparation. Page 2, Measurement and Results table.
summary: A UV7 with 10 mm quartz cells measured cyanocobalamin dissolved in water against a deionized-water blank. The observed peaks were 278.4, 361.0 and 550.4 nm. The mean absorbance ratio at 361 and 550 nm was 3.226.
scope: An identity check for cyanocobalamin in solution. The UV7 produced the reported results. The vendor also lists templates on the UV5Bio and UV5Nano. The study gives no concentration curve for unknowns.
rights: Original catalog summary with a link to the manufacturer's application note.

title: Cyanocobalamin — British Pharmacopoeia Chemical Reference Substance Information Leaflet
locator: Page 1, Declared Content and Additional Information. Page 2, batch identification.
summary: The laboratory assigns content at use by reading a 0.0025% w/v aqueous solution at 361 nm. It specifies a specific absorbance of 207 for a 1% w/v solution in a 1 cm cell and a batch impurity correction of 0.990.
scope: The correction belongs to reference substance batch 4394. Match the leaflet to the bottle before using the material for quantitative work. The leaflet does not identify an instrument model.
rights: Original catalog summary with a link to the Commission's batch leaflet.

title: Cyanocobalamin (Cyanocobalaminum)
version: The International Pharmacopoeia, sixth edition, archived omitted monograph
locator: Page 1, Identity tests A. Page 2, Assay.
summary: The identity test checks three spectral peaks around 278, 361 and 550 nm and their absorbance ratios. The separate quantitative assay calculates cyanocobalamin content from the absorbance of its aqueous solution at about 361 nm with a 1 cm light path.
scope: Historical monograph for cyanocobalamin bulk substance. WHO archives it among its omitted monographs. The assay addresses bulk material rather than total B12 in food or tablets.
rights: Original catalog summary with a link to WHO's archived monograph.

title: Portable low-cost open-source wireless spectrophotometer for fast and reliable measurements
summary: Laganovska and colleagues measured B12 solutions from 3 to 24 ppm at 550 nm on their miniature spectrophotometer and a Shimadzu UVmini-1240. They collected three readings on each of three days. Table 1 gives absorbances and precision for both instruments.
scope: Evidence for choosing a calibration range and examining repeatability with B12 standards. The reported calibration and precision apply to the two instruments and samples tested. The simulated demo requires its own calibration.
rights: Original summary of Laganovska et al. The authors publish the article under CC BY 4.0.

title: Effect of Ascorbic Acid on the Degradation of Cyanocobalamin and Hydroxocobalamin in Aqueous Solution: A Kinetic Study
locator: Spectral Determination and Spectrometric Assay under Materials and Methods. Table I gives the assay characteristics.
summary: Ahmad and colleagues used a Shimadzu UV-1601 with 10 mm quartz cells to follow mixtures of cyanocobalamin and hydroxocobalamin in the presence of ascorbic acid. The assay used 525 and 550 nm together in pH 4 acetate buffer.
scope: Two wavelengths address overlapping absorption from the two cobalamins in this degradation study. A single reading at 550 nm in an unknown mixture cannot identify how much of each form is present.
rights: Original catalog summary with a link to the publisher's article.

title: Challenges in the determination of total vitamin B12 by cyanidation conversion: insights from stable isotope dilution assays
locator: Preparation and concentration determination of standard solutions. Instrumental conditions, UV spectroscopy. Figure 2 compares food chromatograms.
summary: Wang and colleagues checked the concentration of their aqueous cyanocobalamin stock daily. They measured diluted stock at 361 nm on a GENESYS 10S UV-Vis using a 1 cm cuvette and a water blank.
scope: The GENESYS measurement characterized the stock standard. For meat samples the authors used LC-MS/MS and found incomplete recovery of native forms through conversion. Their UV reading alone does not measure total B12 in meat.
rights: Original summary of Wang, Schuster, Asam and Rychlik. The authors publish the article under CC BY 4.0.

title: Evaluation of cyanocobalamin in multivitamin tablets and their Standard Reference Material 3280 by HPLC with visible detection
locator: Authors' abstract, results for NIST SRM 3280 and commercial multivitamin tablets. Journal pages 1609–1613.
summary: Matsumoto and colleagues used liquid chromatography with visible detection on multivitamin tablets. For NIST reference material 3280 they measured 4.64 µg/g cyanocobalamin against a certified value of 4.80 µg/g.
scope: An independent accuracy check in a tablet matrix. The detector measured a chromatographically separated analyte, so directly reading an unseparated tablet extract follows a different method.
rights: Original catalog summary based on the authors' abstract in PubMed.

title: Chemometric determination of vitamin B12 in vitamin B1-6-12 tablets
version: Faculty of Pharmacy special project, academic year 2552 BE (2009)
locator: English abstract, page ข, calibration range and tablet recovery results.
summary: The authors saw linear absorbance at 361 nm for standards from 0 to 40 µg/mL. Their separate multivariate spectral model recovered an average of 100.60% in standard mixtures but 1328.11% in tested B1/B6/B12 tablets.
scope: A university student research project reporting a failed transfer from standards to formulated tablets. The authors found the model unsuitable for quantifying B12 in those tablets.
rights: Original catalog summary with a link to the university's project abstract.
